name: vision_keras_transfer
title: Keras/TF transfer learning: frozen EfficientNet trunk, two-phase fit, compile in a helper - written correctly
origin: domain-vision round 1: the shape the Keras 'Transfer learning & fine-tuning' guide and every production Keras image project share - a tf.data pipeline module, a model factory module, and a train module whose compile() lives in a helper the model is passed into. Added specifically to pin MLV705: the defective keras twin (vision_keras_cnn_bad) cannot pin it, because there the compile helper annotates its parameter and the rule goes quiet.

forbidden.why: the model IS compiled - compile_model() calls model.compile(optimizer=..., loss=..., metrics=[...]) at train.py:47, and run() calls compile_model(model, ...) at train.py:94 before the first fit and again at train.py:106 before the second. The rule's own message ('no compile() call exists anywhere in this workspace') is factually false about this workspace; the only thing that differs from a silent project is that `compile_model`'s first parameter carries no type annotation

the output layer is a bare layers.Dense(num_classes, name='logits') with no activation= at all, which is the correct partner for SparseCategoricalCrossentropy(from_logits=True); no softmax or sigmoid string literal exists in either module
same pairing seen from the loss side - from_logits=True is correct here because the head emits logits

build_datasets() carves the holdout off `base`, which is never shuffled: take()/skip() run on file order, and shuffle() is applied afterwards inside finalize(train_raw, training=True) to the training half only. This is the documented 'split first, shuffle the training half afterwards' guard

augment() is mapped only under `if training:` in finalize(); build_datasets passes training=False for the validation half and build_test_dataset passes training=False, so no random op reaches an evaluation split
run() calls set_seeds() first, which calls keras.utils.set_random_seed(SEED) - the documented TF/Keras seeding entry point that covers Python, numpy and TensorFlow at once
there is no sklearn or torch splitter here; the split is a tf.data take/skip over a deterministic file order, so there is no random_state= or generator= to ask for
this project has no torch DataLoader; the training half is shuffled by tf.data at pipeline.py:54
the evaluation halves go through finalize(..., training=False), which never shuffles
no torch DataLoader and no num_workers anywhere; tf.data parallelism is AUTOTUNE on map()

the metrics are keras.metrics.SparseCategoricalAccuracy and SparseTopKCategoricalAccuracy, which take logits by contract and do their own argmax/topk - they are not sklearn-style metrics fed raw scores
there is no HuggingFace Trainer in this project; both fits pass validation_data= and the run ends in model.evaluate() on a third split
the only schedule is keras.callbacks.ReduceLROnPlateau, which Keras drives itself on epoch end; nothing steps a scheduler by hand
there is no torch.save / torch.load anywhere; persistence is keras ModelCheckpoint and model.export()

gaps.what: model.compile (train.py:47), model.evaluate (train.py:73) and model.export (train.py:82) produce no node, because in each case the receiver is an unannotated function parameter. The whole compile/evaluate/export spine of a Keras project is therefore absent from the diagram.
gaps.evidence: those three ops are labelled and not recovered in either dataflow mode; the two model.fit ops, whose receiver is the local `model` binding in run(), are recovered

gaps.what: compile_model() at train.py:40 is emitted as kind=eval_loop stage=eval and training_callbacks() at train.py:58 as kind=train_loop, though neither function contains a loop
gaps.evidence: node dump: train.py:40 kind=eval_loop level=unit stage=eval label='compile_model()'; train.py:58 kind=train_loop level=unit stage=train label='training_callbacks()'
